name: count
title: Counts the number of occurrences of a specific value

origin.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a specific value in a vector.
origin.usage: count(x, idxs = NULL, value = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector. A matrix is rejected.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

origin.details: Numeric and logical input calls C_count in src/colCounts.c, which treats the vector as one column. A positive index past the end is a missing element. The manual says a count less than .Machine$integer.max is integer and otherwise double. The installed test is count > INT_MAX, so a tally equal to integer.max stays integer.
origin.value: An integer scalar when the count is at most .Machine$integer.max, and a double scalar when it is larger. NA when the count is missing.

translation.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a specific value in a vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 1-d numeric or logical vector. A 2-d array is rejected. Double missing values are nan. Integer missing values are None or -2147483648.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based subscripts. None selects every element. A positive index past the end is a missing element, unlike rows and cols.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A single value to search for. It is coerced to the storage mode of x. TRUE on a numeric vector counts ones.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm.

translation.details: The scan is C_count from matrixStats src/colCounts.c, in the colcounts crate, with what 2 and out-of-bounds indices allowed. The result stays a Python int when the tally is at most 2147483647, including that exact value. A larger tally is a float. None is the missing count.
translation.value: An int at most 2147483647, a float above that, or None when the count is missing.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowcounts import count

count(np.array([2, 1, 2, 3]), value=2)
